guides.title: Americas Trade Before 100 CE: Lithic Highways, Old Copper, Olmec Jade & Andean Spondylus
guides.description: Two continents of pre-100 CE long-distance exchange: Labrador Ramah Chert, Yellowstone–Ohio Hopewell obsidian, California Olivella, Olmec Motagua jadeite, Caral–Chavín Spondylus, and Caribbean Huecoid jade canoes.

guides.title: Mesoamerican & North American Origin Stories: Aztec Five Suns, Maya Popol Vuh, Diné Emergence & Turtle Island
guides.description: Cosmologies of cosmic suns, maize-molded humans, subterranean Emergence worlds, Earth-Diver Turtle Island and Raven traditions across Mesoamerica and North America.

guides.title: Andean, Amazonian & Southern Cone Origin Stories: Viracocha at Lake Titicaca, Pacariqtambo, Huarochirí & the Anaconda Canoe
guides.description: Sacred emergence narratives of stone-sculpted nations at Tiwanaku, the Incas' three windows at Pacariqtambo, the Huarochirí Quechua manuscript, the Tukanoan Ancestral Anaconda, Guarani sacred speech (Ayvu Rapyta) and Mapuche flood peaks.

guides.title: Marks on Stone: Global Wall & Rock Art in Toto
guides.description: Comparative illustrated archive across every inhabited continent—from monumental Paleolithic caves like Lascaux and Sulawesi to desert rock overhangs in Nevada, the Sahara, Australia and Patagonia.

guides.title: Pictographs, Petroglyphs & Painted Caves of North America
guides.description: Continental survey linking >70 North American rock-art complexes—from Winnemucca Lake and Nevada desert overhangs to Lower Pecos murals, Canadian Shield cliffs and Eastern dark-zone caves—to their Indigenous cultures.

guides.title: The children of the high Andes
guides.description: Explore evidence for Inca capacocha, from Llullaillaco and Ampato to El Plomo, Aconcagua and Chuscha.

guides.title: Wallacea to Sahul: Early Hominins, Sea Crossings & Deep-Time Pioneers
guides.description: A million years of strait crossings across Flores, Sulawesi, Timor, Alor, and Raja Ampat leading into Pleistocene Sahul.

guides.title: Pleistocene Australia: Madjedbebe, Kimberley Shelters, Willandra & Arid Pioneers
guides.description: First Nations settlement across tropical Arnhem Land, Kimberley coastlands, Flinders Ranges, and the Murray–Darling lakes from 65,000 years ago onward.

guides.title: Lutruwita / Tasmania: Ice-Age Caves, Bass Strait Separation & Aboriginal Survival
guides.description: 41,600 years of fire ecology, glacial Southwest karst hunting, kelp-vessel engineering, resistance in the Black War, and survival.

guides.title: Continental Trade Routes of Aboriginal Australia: Ochre, Pituri, Greenstone & Pearl Shell
guides.description: Transcontinental kinship exchange highways carrying red ochre, narcotic pituri, Kulin greenstone hatchets, Kimberley pearl shell, and Arnhem–Makassar trade.

guides.title: Conflict & Resistance in Australia: From Pre-Colonial Evidence to the Frontier Wars
guides.description: Bioarchaeological conflict trauma along the Darling River paired with 1794–1900 archaeological and historical records of Frontier Wars resistance.

guides.title: New Guinea & Papua: Highland Agriculture, Bird's Head Pioneers, Hiri & the Kula Ring
guides.description: From 50 ka montane forests and Kuk Swamp wetland drainage to coastal Hiri pottery fleets and Massim *Kula* exchange.

guides.title: Island Melanesia & Lapita: Obsidian Corridors, Villages & Chiefdoms
guides.description: Pleistocene crossings across the Bismarcks and Solomons, ~1200 BCE Lapita expansion to Vanuatu and New Caledonia, and Roviana war-canoe hillforts.

guides.title: Micronesia’s Stone & Coral Worlds: Marianas Latte, Palau, Yap, Nan Madol & Leluh
guides.description: Direct 1500 BCE open-ocean colonization followed by carved volcanic Palau hills, Yap *rai* stone money, Pohnpei basalt islets, and Kosrae coral pyramids.

guides.title: Fiji, Tonga & Samoa: Lapita Foundations, Fortified Chiefdoms & the Tuʻi Tonga Network
guides.description: Lapita settlement at Nukuleka (~900 BCE) through monumental *langi* royal tombs, star mounds at Pulemelei, LiDAR earth forts, and basalt exchange.

guides.title: Aotearoa & Rēkohu: Polynesian Settlement, Pounamu Networks, Pā Fortifications & Wars
guides.description: Rapid ~1280 CE founding settlement, Tūhua obsidian & *pounamu* trade, *pā* hillfort innovation, Musket Wars, New Zealand Wars, and Moriori survival.

guides.title: Central & Eastern Polynesia: Taputapuātea, Eiao Adze Trade, Rapa Iti Forts & Rapa Nui
guides.description: Pan-Polynesian ritual voyages at Raʻiatea, 2,400-km Eiao basalt trade, Rapa Iti stone hilltop *pā*, Mangareva–Pitcairn links, and Rapa Nui resilience.

guides.title: Hawaiʻi: Ahupuaʻa Landscapes, Mauna Kea Quarries, Heiau & Kingdom Unification
guides.description: Alpine basalt workshops at 3,780 m, walled *loko iʻa* fishponds, irrigated taro *loʻi*, monumental *heiau* temples, and Kamehameha I unification.

guides.title: Ibn Battuta’s Twenty-Nine Years Across the Afro-Eurasian World
guides.description: Trace the 1325–1354 CE travels of Tangier jurist Ibn Battuta from Mamluk Cairo and Swahili Kilwa to Delhi, the Maldives, Yuan Quanzhou, and Mali’s court.

guides.title: Indian Ocean Monsoon Trade Before European Sails
guides.description: How predictable seasonal wind reversals bound Red Sea Roman harbors, Swahili stone towns, Malabar pepper ports, Srivijaya, and Fujian shipyards for 1,600 years.

guides.title: The Bantu Expansion Across Sub-Saharan Africa
guides.description: How farming, yam and oil-palm arboriculture, pottery, ironworking, and over 500 related languages transformed half a continent over 3,500 years.

guides.title: Niger–Congo & Bantu Languages: Noun Classes & Continental Reach
guides.description: Explore Africa’s largest language phylum, from Mande and Atlantic–Volta–Niger lineages to the 500+ Bantu tongues linking Cameroon to Cape Town.

guides.title: Afroasiatic & Semitic Languages: From the Nile to Red Sea Scripts
guides.description: How Egyptian, Amazigh (Berber), Cushitic, Chadic, Omotic, and Semitic tongues share triliteral roots spanning five millennia of written history.

guides.title: The Swahili Coast: Coral-Stone Towns of Africa’s Monsoon Shore
guides.description: From eighth-century timber-built fishing villages at Shanga to fourteen-century domed stone architecture and cosmopolitan poetry from Mogadishu to Sofala.

guides.title: West African Sahel & Forest States: Wagadu, Mali, Songhai, Ife & Benin
guides.description: Archaeological towns, Saharan gold–salt corridors, bronze lost-wax guilds, and mud-brick manuscript libraries across West Africa.

guides.title: Ethiopian & Eritrean Highland Traditions: Aksum, Lalibela & Gondar
guides.description: Teff agriculture, Aksumite gold coinage and carved monoliths, Zagwe rock-hewn churches, and Gondar Solomonic libraries across the roof of East Africa.

guides.title: Jenné-jeno and the Inland Niger Delta
guides.description: Excavated flood-plain mounds revealing sub-Saharan Africa’s earliest indigenous clustered urbanism from 250 BCE through historic Jenné.

guides.title: Great Zimbabwe and the Zimbabwe Plateau
guides.description: Monumental dry-stone granite architecture, gold metallurgy, and regional Southern African states across Mapungubwe, Mapela, Great Zimbabwe, and Khami.

guides.title: Aksum, Yeha and the Northern Horn Highlands
guides.description: From Pre-Aksumite temples at Yeha and the Red Sea port of Adulis to Aksum’s monolithic stelae and Lalibela’s medieval rock-hewn churches.

guides.title: Kilwa Kisiwani and the Swahili Coral-Stone Towns
guides.description: Maritime urbanism from sixth-century earth-and-thatch ports at Unguja Ukuu to coral-limestone mosques, coin minting, and the palace of Kilwa Kisiwani.

guides.title: Kerma, Napata and Meroë: Cities of Kush
guides.description: Nearly three millennia of Nubian statehood along the Middle Nile—from Kerma’s mud-brick Deffufa and cattle-tumulus kingdom to Napatan pyramids and Meroitic ironworks.

guides.title: Mecca, the Hijaz and the Hajj Pilgrimage
guides.description: The sanctuary of the Kaaba in Mecca, Medina’s Hijrah landscape, Red Sea crossing ports in Egypt and Sudan, and inland pilgrimage roads across fifteen centuries.

guides.title: Islam: origins, branches, law schools and global networks
guides.description: An introduction to Sunni, Shīʿī (Twelver, Ismāʿīlī, Zaydī), Ibāḍī, legal madhhabs, and Sufi traditions linking Arabia, Africa, the Mediterranean, and Asia.

guides.title: Christianity: early churches, councils, branches and global traditions
guides.description: How Christological councils, imperial politics, monasticisms, African kingdoms, and European Reformations shaped the Church of the East, Oriental Orthodox, Eastern Orthodox, Catholic, Protestant, and independent traditions.

guides.title: Trade on the Mediterranean Sea: ports, shipwrecks and connected civilizations
guides.description: How five millennia of maritime shipping—from Byblos timber ships and the Uluburun wreck to Phoenician-Greek colonies, Roman Portus, Cairo Geniza networks, and Suez—tied Africa, West Asia, and Europe together.

guides.title: Memphis, Giza & Ancient Thebes
guides.description: Trace Old, Middle and New Kingdom Egypt across the northern Memphite pyramid plateau from Giza to Dahshur and southern temple complexes around Karnak, Luxor and Abu Simbel.

guides.title: Timbuktu, Gao & Inland Niger Delta
guides.description: Follow the Niger Bend caravan capitals linking Gold-Coast and Akan forest kola and alluvial gold with Saharan salt caravans and Timbuktu manuscript libraries.

guides.title: Lalibela, Gondar & Harar Jugol
guides.description: Explore Ethiopia’s medieval highland Christian rock-hewn churches at Lalibela, royal basalt castles at Gondar and the walled Islamic caravan city of Harar Jugol.

guides.title: Carthage, Leptis Magna & North Africa
guides.description: Examine Phoenician–Punic Carthage and Kerkuane alongside Imperial Roman–Amazigh civic monuments at Leptis Magna, Timgad, Sabratha, Volubilis and Cyrene.

guides.title: Göbekli Tepe, Çatalhöyük & Hattusha
guides.description: Follow the Anatolian arc from tenth-millennium BCE T-pillar enclosures at Göbekli Tepe and Karahan Tepe to Çatalhöyük’s mudbrick town and Hittite capital Hattusha.

guides.title: Uruk, Ur, Babylon & Nineveh
guides.description: Trace Mesopotamia’s urban core from Eridu and Uruk’s proto-cuneiform temples through Ur’s Royal Cemetery, Hammurabi’s Babylon and Nineveh’s Assyrian libraries.

guides.title: Mohenjo-daro, Harappa & Dholavira
guides.description: Investigate South Asia’s Indus Valley Civilization: civic waterworks, standardized baked bricks, Rakhigarhi’s plains network and Dholavira’s desert reservoirs.

guides.title: Persepolis, Pasargadae & Bisotun
guides.description: Examine the Achaemenid Persian capitals in Fars and Media: Cyrus’s irrigated Paradise gardens at Pasargadae, Darius’s carved Bisotun manifesto and Persepolis’s multi-ethnic reliefs and archives.

guides.title: Petra, Hegra & Palmyra
guides.description: Discover how Nabataean hydraulic engineers at Petra and Hegra and bilingual caravan senators at Palmyra turned arid desert passes into monumental stone capitals.

guides.title: Knossos, Mycenae & Classical Athens
guides.description: Follow the Aegean sequence from Minoan Knossos and Mycenaean Pylos–Mycenae to Archaic and Classical Athens Acropolis, Delphi and Olympia.

guides.title: Pompeii, Imperial Rome & Ostia
guides.description: Connect Rome’s marble imperial fora and apartment insulae at harbor city Ostia Antica with Pompeii and Herculaneum’s 79 CE preserved Campanian streets.

guides.title: Borobudur, Prambanan & Bagan
guides.description: Compare Southeast Asia’s monumental irrigated kingdoms: Sailendra Borobudur and Mataram Prambanan on Central Java alongside Bagan’s thousands of Irrawaddy brick stupas and Óc Eo–Ayutthaya.

guides.title: Early Art & First Settlements of Africa and the Middle East (to 100 BCE)
guides.description: From Middle Stone Age Blombos ochre and Qurta Pleistocene cliffs through Natufian hamlets, Göbekli Tepe, ʿAin Ghazal, Green Sahara pastoralists, Nubian kingdoms, Nok furnaces and Carthage up to 100 BCE.

guides.title: The Congo River: connections, rapids and rainforest histories
guides.description: How a river basin connected communities, divided journeys and shaped settlement, exchange and colonial extraction.

guides.title: Egyptian writing, from hieroglyphs to household letters
guides.description: Follow Egyptian writing down the Nile through carved signs, inked letters, school texts and workers’ accounts.

guides.title: The Rosetta Stone
guides.description: A priestly decree, a multilingual inscription and the route from Rashid to London.

guides.title: Global Genetic Drift, Bottlenecks & Continental Divergence: Africa, Australia, Europe & Americas
guides.description: Why Out-of-Africa founder bottlenecks, ~45,000 years of Sahul isolation, Europe's 3-wave farm-steppe synthesis, and the Beringian Standstill made continents diverge sharply—and what remained shared.

guides.title: Archaic Interbreeding Worldwide: Neanderthals, Denisovans, Ghost Lineages & Adaptive DNA
guides.description: Mapping every continent's inherited archaic DNA—from West African ghost hominins and European–Asian Neanderthal contacts to dual Sahul/Philippine Denisovan pulses, Tibetan EPAS1, and American MUC19.

guides.title: Australopithecus: Every Published Fossil Locality Across Africa
guides.description: Complete species-by-species and basin-by-basin catalogue of 39 published Australopithecus fossil localities across East, Central (Chad), and Southern Africa (~5.0–1.98 Ma).

guides.title: Before 1 Million Years Ago: Every Global Hominin & Tool Site (7.0–1.0 Ma)
guides.description: Exhaustive planetary inventory of 164 hominin fossil and archaeological localities dated older than 1.0 Ma across Africa, the Levant, Caucasus, Europe, Asia, and oceanic Wallacea—plus species attributions and dispersal routes.

guides.title: Where Did We Come From? Origin & Creation Stories Across World Cultures and Religions
guides.description: Master thematic gateway comparing how world religions, Indigenous oral traditions and ancient epics answer 'where did we come from?'—kept carefully distinct from the factual fossil and genomic atlas.

guides.title: African Origin Stories: Ilé-Ifẹ̀, Mande & Dogon Cosmogonies, Ancient Egyptian Creation Centers, Unkulunkulu & ǀKaggen
guides.description: Creation narratives across Africa: Yoruba Odùduwà and Ọbàtálá at Ilé-Ifẹ̀, Mande Niger ordering, Dogon Amma and Nommo, Egyptian Heliopolis/Memphis/Khnum, Baganda Kintu, Kongo Kalûnga, Zulu Uhlanga reeds and San ǀKaggen.

guides.title: Lucy and her world
guides.description: A 3.2-million-year-old skeleton from Hadar, and the fossils and footprints that help explain how her species moved.

guides.title: The branching human family
guides.description: From late Miocene candidates to Homo sapiens, Neanderthals and Denisovans, with the places where the earliest evidence was found.

guides.title: Ten early traces of hominin activity
guides.description: Trackways and stoneworking localities from the African Pliocene to the early occupation of the Chinese Loess Plateau.

guides.title: Laetoli footprint trails
guides.description: Footprints in volcanic ash document upright walking about 3.66 million years ago.

guides.title: Lomekwi 3
guides.description: Large flaked and battered stones from western Lake Turkana date to about 3.3 million years ago.

guides.title: Nyayanga
guides.description: Early Oldowan artifacts, processed animal bones and Paranthropus teeth occur on Kenya’s Homa Peninsula.

guides.title: Namorotukunan
guides.description: Three Oldowan horizons in the northeastern Turkana Basin record toolmaking from about 2.75 to 2.44 million years ago.

guides.title: Bokol Dora 1, Ledi-Geraru
guides.description: Early Oldowan flaking in Ethiopia’s Afar dates to about 2.61–2.58 million years ago.

guides.title: Gona Oldowan localities
guides.description: Several Afar localities preserve some of the best studied Oldowan tools from around 2.6 million years ago.

guides.title: Aïn Boucherit
guides.description: Stone artifacts and butchered bones near Sétif preserve early hominin activity in northern Africa.

guides.title: Hadar’s Makaamitalu localities
guides.description: A younger part of the Hadar sequence preserves Oldowan tools and a maxilla of early Homo.

guides.title: Lower Omo, Shungura Formation
guides.description: Early stone scatters document toolmaking along the lower Omo at about 2.33 million years ago.

guides.title: Shangchen, Chinese Loess Plateau
guides.description: Tool-bearing layers in Shaanxi document early activity outside Africa from about 2.12 million years ago.

guides.title: Africa and the Atlantic islands: linked voyages
guides.description: Ports, passages and return journeys linked to the same dated voyages already shown in the Americas and Pacific atlas.

guides.title: Everyday writing: receipts, complaints and ordinary lives
guides.description: Explore 87 paired originals and translations: food, animals, wages, deliveries, debts, quarrels and invitations across the ancient world and colonial Americas.

guides.title: Greenland / Kalaallit Nunaat — homelands, farms and colonial harbours
guides.description: From early Arctic camps to Inuit communities, Norse settlements and nineteenth-century connections.

guides.title: Iceland — settlement, assemblies and an enduring population
guides.description: Follow the settlement landscape, legal institutions, church, trade and nineteenth-century Reykjavík.

guides.title: Faroe Islands — early livestock, ocean connections and local institutions
guides.description: A whole-archipelago study from pre-Norse evidence to the end of the trade monopoly and nineteenth-century change.

guides.title: England from ice-age landscapes to 1900
guides.description: Early people, Roman towns, port cities, industry and reform across England.

guides.title: Wales from the first people to 1900
guides.description: Cave archaeology, maritime exchange, Welsh polities, language, coal and slate.

guides.title: Scotland and its islands through 1900
guides.description: Mainland and island histories from hunter-gatherers to medieval polities, mills, crofting and rail.

guides.title: Ireland from early settlement to 1900
guides.description: An island-wide guide to prehistoric settlement, medieval Ireland, plantation, famine and land reform.

guides.title: Ulster and the north of Ireland through 1900
guides.description: Early settlement, Gaelic and Anglo-Norman sites, plantations, dissent and manufacturing in the north.

guides.title: Early people and changing landscapes of Britain and Ireland
guides.description: Footprints, cave remains and hearths from intermittent Pleistocene activity to postglacial settlement.

guides.title: Lascaux and the Vézère Valley
guides.description: Upper Paleolithic cave art, the evidence for its age, and the landscape around the original cave and its replicas.

guides.title: The Roman Empire
guides.description: A Mediterranean-wide guide to Roman expansion, provincial life and the empire’s transformation in Late Antiquity.

guides.title: Roman Expansion and Frontiers
guides.description: How conquest, bridges, garrisons and local settlements shaped the outer provinces of the Roman Empire.

guides.title: Roman Cities, Trade and People
guides.description: Harbours, streets, inscriptions and letters show how goods moved and how people lived across the Roman world.

guides.title: Late Antiquity and the Eastern Roman Empire
guides.description: Changes of rule in the West, continuity at Constantinople, and the changing place of North Africa and the eastern Mediterranean.

guides.title: Hadrian’s Wall
guides.description: The Tyne–Solway frontier, its forts and crossing points, and the communities whose lives continued around it.

guides.title: Stonehenge and Its Landscape
guides.description: The stone circle, earthworks and burial monuments of Salisbury Plain, and what the stones reveal about their origins.

guides.title: Ahmad ibn Fadlan: the 921–922 CE Volga Embassy (Reality vs. Eaters of the Dead)
guides.description: What really happened on the 4,000-km Abbasid diplomatic mission from Baghdad across Khwarazm and the steppes to Volga Bulgaria and Viking Rus merchants—and how Michael Crichton adapted it into fiction.

guides.title: Shipwrecks of Antiquity: Sunken Hulls & Maritime Worlds
guides.description: How ancient and medieval shipwrecks across the Mediterranean, Nile, Red Sea, North Atlantic, Indian Ocean, and East China Sea preserve exact sinking dates, hull engineering, and lost cargoes.

guides.title: Superlative Shipwrecks: The Oldest, the Deepest & the Only Examples of Their Kind
guides.description: Earth's extraordinary benchmark shipwrecks—from the oldest planked boats and Uluburun to the 6,895 m deep USS Samuel B. Roberts, Shackleton's Endurance, Sweden's raised Vasa, and one-of-a-kind archaeological time capsules.

guides.title: Endurance (1915/2022) & Vasa (1628/1961): Polar Ice, Baltic Hubris & Intact Survival
guides.description: The story of Ernest Shackleton's Endurance (discovered 3,008 m under Weddell Sea ice in March 2022) and Sweden's 1628 royal warship Vasa (which turtled in Stockholm Harbor and was raised whole in 1961).

guides.title: Graveyards of the Sea: Golden Gate, Columbia Bar, Cape Hatteras & Global Chokepoints
guides.description: Why sailors kept forcing the world's deadliest maritime chokepoints—from San Francisco's Golden Gate, Columbia River Bar, Cape Hatteras, and the Great Lakes to Cape Horn, Namibia's Skeleton Coast, Agulhas, Scilly, and Western Australia.

guides.title: Indo-European Languages: Steppes, Anatolia & the Hybrid Origin Debate
guides.description: How Sanskrit, Greek, Latin, Celtic, Slavic, Iranian, Germanic, and Hittite branched across Eurasia—and what 2023 linguistics and archaeogenomics reveal.

guides.title: Hannibal: the campaign and the elephants
guides.description: A dated journey across Iberia, the Alps, Italy and North Africa, separating ancient accounts from archaeological evidence and disputed routes.

guides.title: Ötzi and the Copper Age Alps
guides.description: Read the archaeological evidence from one traveller’s equipment, last meals, body and Alpine findspot.

guides.title: People preserved in cold landscapes
guides.description: Compare glacier recoveries, dry Arctic graves and ice-filled Altai burial chambers across the Northern Hemisphere.

guides.title: Homo neanderthalensis: Every Mapped Fossil & aDNA Locality Across Eurasia
guides.description: Comprehensive Eurasian atlas of 121 confirmed Neanderthal skeletal, dental, and ancient-DNA localities from Portugal, Gibraltar, Wales, and submerged Doggerland across Europe, Crimea, Caucasus, Levant, and Zagros to Uzbekistan and Altai Siberia (~430–37 ka).

guides.title: Sweden from Ice Age tools to 1900
guides.description: Postglacial movement, Iron Age central places and Baltic trade, mining, factories and the growth of cities.

guides.title: Sápmi across borders, from early landscapes to 1900
guides.description: Sámi communities, livelihoods and rights across Varanger, the Scandinavian interior and the Kola Peninsula.

guides.title: Svalbard from the earliest documented voyages to 1900
guides.description: Bear Island, shore whaling stations, Pomor and Norwegian wintering, polar expeditions, tourism and early coal claims.

guides.title: Denmark from Ice Age hunters to 1900
guides.description: Jutland and island communities, early markets, Sound shipping, overseas commerce, urban growth and rural cooperation.

guides.title: Finland from the earliest secure camps to 1900
guides.description: Postglacial settlements, lake and coastal economies, medieval towns, new institutions and nineteenth-century work.

guides.title: Norway from postglacial camps to 1900
guides.description: Coastal settlements, inland mines, trading wharves and the growth of political and industrial institutions.

guides.title: Near Eastern, Abrahamic & European Origin Stories: Atrahasis, Genesis & Qur'anic Creation, Bundahishn, Hesiod & the Eddas
guides.description: Creation traditions from Sumerian–Babylonian cuneiform tablets, Jewish, Christian and Islamic scriptures (Genesis and Qur'an), Zoroastrian Bundahishn, Greek Hesiod/Prometheus and Norse Eddas.

guides.title: The Picts, their kingdoms and the emergence of Alba
guides.description: Origins, language, settlements, conflicts and the changing names of power in early medieval northern Britain.

guides.title: Scotland’s standing stones, settlements and tombs
guides.description: A map of regional monument traditions, with guides to Orkney, Shetland, Calanais and Kilmartin Glen.

guides.title: Neolithic Orkney’s houses, tombs and stone circles
guides.description: From Skara Brae and the Brodgar isthmus to the settlements and chambered tombs of the outer islands.

guides.title: Shetland’s early farms, standing stones and brochs
guides.description: A mapped history from coastal middens, the houses and fields of West Mainland, and Unst’s standing stones to later Iron Age and Norse settlements.

guides.title: Calanais and the stone settings of Loch Roag
guides.description: The Lewis stone circle, avenue and burial cairn in a wider landscape of ridges, lochs and satellite monuments.

guides.title: Kilmartin Glen’s cairns, stone settings and rock art
guides.description: A valley-wide guide from the linear cemetery and Temple Wood to carved rock above the watershed and the later stronghold of Dunadd.

guides.title: Europe: departures, returns and American connections
guides.description: Ports, passages and return journeys linked to the same dated voyages already shown in the Americas and Pacific atlas.

guides.title: Sino-Tibetan Languages: Yellow River Millet Farmers to Over 400 Tongues
guides.description: How one ancestral family split into Sinitic literary traditions, Tibetan plateau writing, and dozens of Himalayan–Burmese Tibeto-Burman languages.

guides.title: Austronesian Languages: From Taiwan Across Half the Globe’s Oceans
guides.description: Double-outrigger voyagers connecting Taiwanese Formosan mountain roots through the Philippines, Indonesia, Polynesia, and Madagascar.

guides.title: Dravidian & Austroasiatic Languages Across South and Mainland SE Asia
guides.description: Tracing South Asia’s ancient Dravidian root tongues (Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Brahui) alongside Munda–Khmer Austroasiatic river civilizations.

guides.title: Steppe & Silk Road Oasis Cultures Across Inner Eurasia
guides.description: Nomadic horse-riding confederations from Scythians and Xiongnu to Sogdians, Turkic Khaganates, and Timurid Samarkand.

guides.title: South Asian Classical Traditions: Maurya, Gupta, Chola & Mughal Worlds
guides.description: From Ashokan rock pillars and Nalanda logic halls to Chola bronzes, Ajanta murals, and Indo-Persian architecture.

guides.title: East Asian Literate Traditions: Grand Canal, Hangeul, Kyoto & Edo Crafts
guides.description: Movable woodblock and metal type, civil-service libraries, ceramic kilns, and coastal urban culture linking China, Korea, Vietnam, and Japan.

guides.title: Siberia, the Urals & Altai: Ice Age Mammoth Hunters to Scythian Frozen Barrows
guides.description: Over 200,000 years across northern Eurasia: Kapova murals, Denisova and Okladnikov hominins, Mal'ta–Yana mammoth hunters, Lake Baikal cemeteries, and frozen Pazyryk horse-lord tombs.

guides.title: Rus, Volga & Muscovy: Birch-Bark Republics, Timber Craft & Imperial Synthesis
guides.description: From Staraya Ladoga and Novgorod birch-bark letters to Volga Bulgaria, white-stone Vladimir–Suzdal cathedrals, Moscow Kremlin, and the Great Abatis Line.

guides.title: Across Siberia by River & Tea Caravan: Tobolsk, Mangazeya, Irkutsk, Kiakhta & Amur
guides.description: How river portages, Arctic kogge ships, *ostrog* stockades, and the 1727 Kiakhta Tea Road connected the Urals and Moscow across all of North Asia to Kamchatka and the Pacific.

guides.title: The Great Wall of China (Changcheng): Multi-Millennium Frontier Ecology & Stone Ramparts
guides.description: Not a single continuous wall, but two millennia of Qi, Zhao, Qin, Han, Northern Wei, Jin, and Ming walls, signal beacons, water-gates, and regulated horse-for-tea market towns.

guides.title: China's Dynastic Capitals & Grand Canal: Hydraulic States from Erlitou to Ming–Qing
guides.description: Tracing 4,000 years of urban continuity and canal engineering—from Shimao, Erlitou, and Anyang to Chang'an, Kaifeng, Hangzhou, Nanjing, Jingdezhen, Pingyao, and Beijing.

guides.title: Mongolia: Deer Stones, Xiongnu, Orkhon Turks, Uyghurs & Mobile Urbanism Beyond 1206
guides.description: Over 45,000 years on the Eastern Steppe—Tolbor blades, flying-stag deer stones, Xiongnu ironworks and royal silk barrows, Göktürk runic steles, Uyghur Ordu-Baliq, Khitan towns, and Buddhist monasteries.

guides.title: Japan's Three Shogunates: Kamakura, Muromachi & Tokugawa Bakufu (1185–1868)
guides.description: Seven centuries of dual imperial-and-warrior rule: from Kamakura legal codes and Hakata Bay Mongol defense through Ashikaga Kyoto, Sekigahara, and Edo's Tōkaidō *sankin-kōtai* highways.

guides.title: Japanese Castles & Ryukyuan Gusuku: Timber Tenshu Keeps, Stone Ramparts & Castle Towns
guides.description: Engineering monumental *ishigaki* stone slopes and multi-tiered wooden *tenshu* across Azuchi, Osaka, Himeji, Matsumoto, Inuyama, Hikone, Matsue, Kumamoto, Nijō, and Okinawa's limestone *gusuku*.

guides.title: Korea: Paleolithic Valleys, Three Kingdoms Gold, Metal Type & Joseon Mountain Citadels
guides.description: From Seokjang-ni and Jeongok-ri Pleistocene terraces, Bangudae whaling cliffs, and dolmen cemeteries to Goguryeo Yalu citadels, Silla Gyeongju, 1377 *Jikji* metal type, and Joseon Hwaseong–Imjin defenses.

guides.title: Himalaya & Tea Horse Road (Chama Gudao): Denisovans, Mountain Passes & Bhutan Dzongs
guides.description: How brick tea, pashmina wool, Tibetan salt, Newar silver, and Himalayan genomics crossed 5,000-meter passes from Pu'er and Chengdu to Lhasa, Kathmandu, Thimphu, Ladakh, and Hunza.

guides.title: Central Asia: Kazakhstan to Afghanistan Across BMAC Oases, Bactria & Silk Caravan Passes
guides.description: Country-by-country across Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Afghanistan: Botai, Gonur Depe, Sarazm, Shortugai, Ai-Khanoum, Samarkand, Bukhara, Khiva, Tash Rabat, and Herat.

guides.title: Southeast Asia & the Spice Islands: Early Hominins, Jade Voyagers, Maritime Entrepôts & Maluku
guides.description: From Java–Flores–Luzon hominins and Tam Pà Ling/Lenggong caves through Ban Chiang bronze, Funan–Óc Eo, Champa, Srivijaya, Majapahit, Brunei Kota Batu, Manila, and the Maluku clove-nutmeg networks.

guides.title: Buddhist temples, monasteries and networks
guides.description: From early Indian stupas to pilgrimage, scholarship and temple patronage across Asia.

guides.title: Confucian temples, learning and government
guides.description: From Confucius and Mencius to academies, examinations and ritual across East Asia.

guides.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls: manuscripts, caves and the lives around them
guides.description: Read the scrolls as ancient physical objects, a diverse body of Jewish writings, and part of a wider desert archive of everyday documents.

guides.title: The Terracotta Army and Qin imperial mausoleum
guides.description: A buried army, an imperial tomb and the workshops and labor force that built the First Emperor’s funerary landscape.

guides.title: Angkor Wat and the waters of Greater Angkor
guides.description: A Khmer temple, its inhabited enclosure and the engineered landscape between Phnom Kulen and Tonlé Sap.

guides.title: The Taj Mahal and Mughal Agra’s Yamuna riverfront
guides.description: The Mughal garden-tomb in its setting of river terraces, irrigated gardens, markets and the imperial Agra Fort.

guides.title: Chinese Explorers, Envoys & Geographers: Zhang Qian to Zheng He and Xu Xiake
guides.description: Two millennia of Chinese overland diplomacy, Buddhist pilgrimage epics, Abbasid-captive African travelogues, Mongol-era embassies to Europe, oceanic voyages and scientific karst surveys (138 BCE–1640 CE).

guides.title: Saudi Arabia & the Arabian Peninsula (1000 BCE–1900 CE): Incense Oases, Nabataeans, Caliphates & Diriyah
guides.description: Systematic regional synthesis of Arabian history across three millennia: Taymāʾ and Dadān, Maʾrib and Sabaʾ, Qaryat al-Fāw, Nabataean Hegra, Himyarite Ḥimā, Abbasid Darb Zubaydah, Al-Aḥsāʾ, Historic Jeddah, Oman, and Diriyah/Riyadh.

guides.title: India Across Three Millennia: Mahajanapadas, Maurya & Gupta Empires, Southern Kingdoms, Sultanates, Mughals, Ahom & Sikh Polities
guides.description: Comprehensive chronological and regional guide answering who, where and when across South Asia—from Painted Grey Ware and Magadha through Ashoka, Satavahanas, Guptas, Nalanda, Pallavas, Chalukyas, Cholas, Delhi & Bengal Sultanates, Vijayanagara, Mughals, Ahom Assam and the Sikh Empire.

guides.title: North Sentinel Island & the Sentinelese: Reef Uplift, Isolation & Indian Ocean History
guides.description: The Sentinelese of the Andaman Islands: inferred Andamanese deep-time ancestry without direct DNA, unclassified language, salvaged shipwreck ironworking, India's legal non-contact buffer, and the 2004 earthquake uplift.

guides.title: The Quest for Blue & Ancient Dyes: Pigments, Snails, Bugs, Poison & Global Trade
guides.description: How humanity's obsession with rare blues, royal purples, and bright crimsons—from lapis lazuli in Badakhshan, Egyptian Blue, Han Blue, and Maya Blue to Phoenician sea snails, Oaxaca cochineal, poisonous arsenic greens, and 1856 Mauveine—drove trade, espionage, conquest, and modern chemistry.

guides.title: Chinese Ceramics & Porcelain: 20,000 Years from Xianrendong Clay to Global Blue-and-White
guides.description: How Chinese potters invented the world's oldest fired clay pots (~18,000 BCE), glazed high-temperature stoneware, true white translucent kaolin porcelain (Xing/Jingdezhen), and Silk Road cobalt blue-and-white export empires.

guides.title: Chinese Gunpowder & Explosives: From Tang Daoist Elixirs to Global Artillery
guides.description: How Daoist immortality alchemists chasing elixirs in 9th-century China stumbled upon saltpeter-sulfur-charcoal black powder—launching Song fire arrows, iron thunder-crash bombs, 1280s metal guns, Mongol Eurasian transmission, and the modern world.

guides.title: Genghis Khan: conquest, camps and cities
guides.description: Dated campaigns, archaeological settlements and changing territorial reconstructions, with the limits of the chronicles kept visible.

guides.title: Mesopotamia and the lives written on clay
guides.description: Follow cuneiform across the Tigris and Euphrates, from early accounts at Uruk to merchants’ letters, school exercises and the collections at Nineveh.

guides.title: Indigenous Australian Origin Stories: The Dreaming (Tjukurpa, Wangarr, Bugarrigarra, Nyitting & Lutruwita)
guides.description: Sacred creation, Songline and emergence accounts across Arnhem Land, Central & Western Deserts, Kimberley, Southeast Australia, Noongar Southwest, Tasmania (Lutruwita) and Torres Strait — documented from public Indigenous, ethnographic and literary collections.

guides.title: South Asian, East Asian & Pacific Origin Stories: Vedic Hymns, Pangu & Nüwa, Kojiki, Dangun & Polynesian Cosmogonies
guides.description: How South Asian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Oceanic sacred literatures explain cosmic emergence, primordial giants, clay-molded humans and sky-earth separation.

guides.title: Marco Polo: journey, cities and a difficult book
guides.description: A dated reading of Polo’s reported travels, the world he described and the evidence behind the map.

guides.title: Silk Roads: changing networks of towns, ports and people
guides.description: Selected land and sea connections from Han-era cities to fourteenth-century merchant instructions, grounded in dated evidence.

guides.title: Hindu and Muslim histories in South Asia
guides.description: From Malabar’s merchant ports to Mughal courts and colonial Punjab, Hindu and Muslim lives intersected through trade, worship, law, political alliances and conflict.

guides.title: Tibet and the Dalai Lama institution
guides.description: How a reincarnation lineage became a center of government, shaped Tibetan religious and social life, and continued in exile.

guides.title: Asia and the Pacific: the other shores of the voyages
guides.description: Ports, passages and return journeys linked to the same dated voyages already shown in the Americas and Pacific atlas.
